result.summary: The image shows a one-way residential street with sidewalks on both sides and a marked bike lane. While the environment is generally walkable with mature trees and a buffer of parked cars, it lacks dedicated pedestrian crossing infrastructure and features some sidewalk obstructions.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is located directly in the path of the right-side sidewalk, narrowing the accessible width for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No marked pedestrian crossings are visible in the immediate vicinity, which may encourage unsafe mid-block crossing behavior.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks at the nearest intersections to provide safe, designated crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions (bulb-outs) at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Speed Management
interventions.description: Introduce traffic calming measures such as speed humps to ensure low vehicle speeds on this residential street.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked zebra crosswalk and continuous sidewalks, though these lack a protective buffer from the roadway. The wide street and faded pavement markings suggest a design that prioritizes vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The zebra stripes are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Lack of traffic control
hazards.description: The intersection lacks visible stop signs or signals, relying on driver yielding at a wide crossing.

hazards.name: Utility pole at corner
hazards.description: The pole is located at the corner, potentially narrowing the effective sidewalk width and obstructing sightlines.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility ladder or continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve the visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking near the intersection to ensure clear sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-leg intersection with minimal pedestrian infrastructure beyond a single marked crosswalk. The environment is dominated by asphalt, with long crossing distances and a lack of visible traffic signals or pedestrian-specific safety features.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide intersection requires pedestrians to spend significant time in the roadway without a refuge island.

hazards.description: The existing zebra crossing is faded, reducing its visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and trees near the corner may block sightlines between pedestrians and turning motorists.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features wide sidewalks and a marked crosswalk at a corner, but safety is compromised by a significant blind corner created by the building's placement.
